text:
maria: heads up — noticed a host hitting KV cache saturation (~95%) during the 10:12 window. tenant 'A' had ~60% residency and we started seeing paging thrash + reallocation churn :eyes:
jasper: can you paste the pprof/alloc snapshot?
maria: here's the short pprof top output i grabbed quickly:
```
pprof: heap1
  45.2%  45.2%  tenant_A: kv_pages (residency 62%)
  25.0%  70.2%  tenant_B: kv_pages (residency 18%)
  10.1%  80.3%  tenant_C: kv_pages (residency 7%)
  19.7% 100.0%  misc: slab_frag + transient allocations
```
maria: we also saw a spike in pagewalks in the kernel logs around the same time: "kmem: pagefaults high, swap-in backlog 120"
liam: interesting — any recent runtime changes? kernel selection or batching heuristics landed last deploy, right?
jasper: yeah, we rolled kernel-selector v2 yesterday (optimizes fused-attn kernels). Hypothesis: changed memory access stride -> worse slab reuse causing fragmentation for longctx traces.
liam: that would explain lower temporal locality. eviction policy currently LRU-ish + tenant quota soft-limit (we only enforce above 90%). so noisy tenant A can bleed until host saturation then everyone suffers.
maria: proposed quick experiment: enable per-tenant soft-watermark smoothing + early compaction pass when host > 80%. label: kv-smooth-v1
jasper: sounds good. specifics?
maria: plan: 1) admit smoothing that clamps per-tenant residency growth rate (delta per min) 2) trigger background slab-compact when host_residency > 80% (low-priority, rate-limited) 3) add short-term eviction bias for tenants exceeding smoothed quota (prefetch-safe evicts)
liam: +1. Add telemetry for "resident_delta_per_min" and "compaction_cycles". want to compare before/after p95 latency and pagewalks.
sre-bot: incident-note: created ticket RNW-4521 "kv saturation: tenant residency smoothing experiment" assigned to eng-runtime.
jasper: i'll wire the feature flag (kv.smooth.v1) behind rollout and start on a canary fleet of 5 hosts.
maria: also adding a regression check — after kernel-selector rollout we should run a microbench that simulates longctx traces to measure reuse ratio (hits / accesses). suspect reuse_ratio dropped ~12% in yesterday's post-deploy run.
liam: if our hypothesis holds, we should consider fallback: if reuse_ratio < threshold, route longctx requests to a compatibility kernel that preserves previous access pattern.
jasper: noted. will add fallback policy to router (route-compat-longctx).
maria: for immediate mitigation i'll patch quota to hard-start at 85% host -> earlier evict handoff. should reduce emergency paging.
liam: timeline?
maria: patch + canary tonight, collect metrics for 4h, then expand.
jasper: logging snippet i'll add to the rollout to make root-cause easier:
```
log: "kv_smooth: tenant=%s prior_resid=%d new_resid=%d action=%s"
```
maria: neat. post results in this thread, please. if compaction causes CPU regressions we'll need to tune rate. :loudspeaker:
infra-bot: deploy job queued: canary/kv-smooth-v1 on 5 hosts (ETA 00:30).
liam: thanks all. TL;DR: tenant A caused KV saturation after kernel-selector change -> fragmentation / reuse drop. Experiment kv-smooth-v1 to smooth residency growth + early compaction + eviction bias. Monitoring: reuse_ratio, pagewalks, p95 latency.
maria: thanks — will report back after the 4h window. :thumbsup:
